newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ex-rebel promises "miracle" in south Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Ex-rebel promises "miracle" in south Philippines.

text.p: A former Moslem rebel who plunged the southern Philippines into a bloody civil war has vowed to "cajole the genie of war" back into its bottle and turn Mindanao island into an economic miracle.

A week after being elected governor of a semi-autonomous Moslem region, Nur Misuari is now in the thick of a new battle -- to win over Christian Filipinos and get them to support his programme to rebuild an area battered by 24 years of war.
"Brothers and sisters, give us...time and we are going to produce (a) miracle," the former rebel chieftain said on Saturday in a meeting with Christian businessmen in southern Butuan city.
Misuari, who signed a peace deal with Manila on September 2, said he was confident Mindanao could catch up with the country's prosperous Christian areas "in 10 to 20 years".
"I believe this is the best gift that we could give to you."
President Fidel Ramos attended the conference as part of his own campaign to soften Christian opposition to the accord which ended a separatist war that killed more than 120,000 people.
In Manila on Friday, after he was proclaimed governor of a region comprising four impoverished Moslem provinces, Misuari said he did not want "another era of darkness and bloodshed" in Mindanao.
"We are going to invite investments from the world community. If I can exorcise the spectre of war, the genie of war and cajole it to go back to its bottle, it will be good for all of us."
The accord involves setting up a rebel-led Southern Philippines Council for Peace and Development (SPCPD) to oversee development of 14 provinces, mostly dominated by Christians.
It envisages the council as a precursor to an expanded autonomous area to include even Christian provinces voting to join it in a referendum in three years time.

Some Christians virulently oppose the deal and have formed vigilante squads to fight it. Although the country's five million Moslem minority regard Mindanao as their ancenstral homeland, they are now outnumbered 3-to-1 by Christians.

Suspected vigilantes on Friday lobbed a grenade at the southern Zamboanga city hall, shattering glass panels but causing no casualties, police said. The city's Christian mayor is among local officials who support the peace deal.
Mindanao Business Council (MBC) chairman Sebastian Angliongto said Mindanao businessmen continued to have reservations about the peace deal but "would rather look at the positive".
"Of course there are some uncertainties...(but) businessmen look for opportunity...Give us peace, we will know what to do," he told reporters.

The MBC pledged at the Butuan meeting 14 billion pesos ($538 million) in investments for various projects, mostly in areas outside the SPCPD zone. They included rehabilitation of a nickel mining project in mainly Christian Surigao.
Manila business leader Vicente Paterno said there was in general an upbeat attitude towards Misuari among businessmen he talked with.
But among some, "it seems the attitude ranges from very positive to pragmatic...and all the way to hostility," he said.

The Ramos administration has said it is allocating 32.6 billion pesos ($1.2 billion) of the national budget for next year to the SPCD region. This is on top of 10 billion pesos ($385 million) Ramos ordered released for various projects in the area this year.
